name: create-data-type-alias
description: A data type authored through the generic change set. The implementation types (`data_types` until contract `8.0.0`, `implementation_types` since) are a full model layer with a schema, a reader, a writer and ARXML output, and no MCP tool of their own. Here it is one `create` at an `implementation_types` element address, with no new tool and no new parameter.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model, whose `base_types` layer (`data_types/base/`) already holds the base type `float32_base`. The value type rests on it and refines it with a unit and a value range. A value type's `base` must name a declared `base_type` — the reference-role rule, which `check-model` reports and pass D refuses — and `float32_base` is one.

authorization.notes: Scope is keyed by operation and address. Nothing in it names a tool, which is why an operation on a layer that never had one needs no scope vocabulary of its own.

input.intent: Add the VehicleSpeed_kph value type so speed signals carry a unit and a declared range.

value.name: VehicleSpeed_kph
value.description: Vehicle speed in kilometres per hour

after.name: VehicleSpeed_kph
after.description: Vehicle speed in kilometres per hour

expected.notes: `staged` is the reviewable state: the change set is validated against the staged result — the value type's `base` resolves to a declared base type, and the exporter generates no `SHORT-NAME` from a value type's name at all since contract `7.0.0` retired the application view it used to invent, so nothing lengthens this one against the 128-character `Identifier` limit — and commit later applies exactly this delta. The real model is still byte-identical at this point.
